inputs.root_cause: XLIFF-PRESERVE-001's 4 obligations (unknown constructs preserved; absent-vs-explicit-default distinction; explicit lossless-vs-canonical caller choice; loss-report API) were all unexamined, sharing an identical generic 6-symbol citation. Investigation found: unknown-content preservation is fully built and tested (ExtensionNode stores raw bytes); absent-vs-default is proven for one field (Note.priority) via a presence-checked-before-parse pattern; the explicit lossless/canonical choice and loss-report API are both confirmed architecturally absent -- dumps()/dump() have no mode parameter and there is no LossReport-equivalent class anywhere in the package, matching an identical finding for UBL's parallel obligations investigated earlier this session.

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed xliff's remaining capabilities. XLIFF-PRESERVE-001 was 4/4 unresolved, all sharing an identical generic 6-symbol citation with no obligation-specific test selectors, unlike most of the capabilities already swept this session.

2. Investigated obligation 1 (unknown constructs preserved): ExtensionNode.xml stores an unrecognized namespaced subtree as raw bytes, not a typed reconstruction. Found test_semantic_roundtrip_preserves_unknown_namespace_and_order already proving a vendor extension element survives a full load-dump-load-dump cycle byte-identical. Ran it directly: passed. Promoted.

3. Investigated obligation 3 (explicit lossless-vs-canonical caller choice) and obligation 4 (loss-report API before saving): grepped writer.py for a mode/preservation parameter and the whole package for a LossReport/check_preservation-style class -- found neither. dumps()/dump() have exactly one output path with no separate canonical-regeneration mode, so there is nothing for an explicit choice to select between, and no reporting API exists to describe what such a regeneration would drop. Corrected both from a misleading generic `partial` citation to an honest `missing` naming the confirmed architectural gap -- the same gap independently found in UBL's parallel obligations this session (both packages serialize a raw XmlNode/ExtensionNode tree with a single output path).

4. Investigated obligation 2 (absent-vs-explicit-default distinction): found reader.py's note-parsing checks `if "priority" in note.attrib:` before parsing, so an absent priority leaves Note.priority as None rather than a defaulted numeric value. Found test_note_priority_and_category_are_represented already proving this ([1, 5, None] for three notes, the third lacking the attribute). Ran it directly: passed. Promoted the citation but kept status `partial` (not `implemented`) and narrowed source/tests to only this one field, since the claim was verified for Note.priority specifically, not systematically swept across every optional field in the model -- an honest scope limitation rather than an overclaim.
